subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

reply.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

observed.facings.png: A 4x4 linked atlas, downscaled, on a checkerboard. It shows thin copper pipes with green verdigris mottling: elbows, straight runs, tees and a cross with round bolted grey-steel bosses domed in copper at the junctions, grey clamp-collar end caps on the dead ends, and a lone boss cell. No backdrop.
observed.south.png: The same atlas at full resolution (1408 px). The tube is uniform in width, about 36 px, with a dark outline, a lit centre highlight and fine orange/teal oxidation grain that is symmetric across the axis. The elbows bend smoothly on the axis. Each junction boss is a riveted steel ring around a hammered copper dome, with a small bent tab and a scrap plate under one edge. The end caps are grey ribbed hose-clamp collars with a domed bolted cap; their orientation matches each dead end's direction. Clean alpha, no shadow.
observed.single.png: Identical to south.png: the full 4x4 atlas at high resolution, sharp, clean cut-out.
observed.scale.png: An offline render at 96 px/cell on a brown checker floor: a 14-cell network with two tees, two elbows, three end caps and a lone boss, with a vanilla pawn to the right for scale. The pipe is a thin copper line, far narrower than the pawn and flat on the ground. Joints are seamless. Small grey wire-wrap and patch-plate hardware appears irregularly on some straight cells.
observed.siblings.png: Reference only: the industrial sibling pipe is the same layout drawn as a thin grey steel line, about the same width and draw size as the Scrapper candidate.
observed.variants_1.png: The strip of straight variants: a long horizontal strip with a wire-wrap-and-hose-clamp and a riveted grey patch plate, plus four vertical cells (two plain stretches with different grain, one wire wrap with clamp, one patch plate). Each vertical cell ends at the same width and position as the atlas straight. A few stray dark specks of pixels float just off the patch plates (around x≈1254 y≈145 in the horizontal strip and x≈1262 y≈550 beside the vertical one), and the vertical patch plate juts slightly past the left tube edge.
observed.assembled_1.png: The same 96 px/cell network render without the pawn. The variant hardware is irregularly spaced (one wrap on the upper vertical, one on the right of the main run, one wrap on the middle drop, one patch plate on the right drop). No obvious repeat from cell to cell, and every joint between cells is continuous.
observed.assembled_2.png: The network at 48 px/cell. It still reads clearly as a copper pipe with dark bosses at the tees, small dark caps at the ends and small grey bands of hardware. At this size the hardware dots are tiny grey marks.
observed.assembled_3.png: A zoomed crop at 150 px/cell showing a tee up, an elbow and a tee down. Sharp, not blurry. The grain varies along the run. A wire wrap shows on the vertical and on the right-hand run, and the bolted bosses centre exactly on the junctions. The end cap's clamp collar and dome are crisp. The pipe width matches across every cell boundary with no seams.

CAMERA.seen: Flat ground art seen top-down, as the card's engine limits require for Graphic_Linked pipes. The boss domes and the end caps have soft top lighting consistent with the floor plane. No side elevation.

BORE.seen: No open bore shows anywhere. Every dead end is closed by a clamp collar and domed cap, and the tube runs flat in the floor plane.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1/2/3 each cell's pipe meets its neighbour at the cell edge on the same axis, with the same width and centre line. Tees, elbows and variant straights join without steps or seams.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Pipe ends sit exactly at the cell-edge midpoints where neighbours exist. There are no stray connector stubs, and dead ends are capped rather than left as open stubs.

LAYERS.seen: A single-layer floor part. The bosses draw over the tube at junctions and the hardware draws over the tube. Nothing is drawn behind what it should cover.

ROTATIONS.seen: One atlas, as the engine allows. Every tile and variant uses the same copper/verdigris palette, tube width and grey-steel hardware.

SIGNATURE.seen: Reads as a linked floor pipe with straight runs, elbows, tees, a cross, end caps and a lone cell. It has the described bolted scrap-plate bosses, clamp-collar caps, and wire-wrap and patch-plate variants on roughly one straight cell in four.

MATERIAL.seen: The tube reads as oxidised copper: a specular centre highlight, mottled verdigris and pitting. The bosses and caps read as worn grey steel with rivets.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The tube is 36 px of a 264 px cell, centred on the cell axis. Junction bosses stay inside the cell. Nothing overflows.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out with no backdrop or cast shadow, apart from a few isolated stray dark specks next to the patch-plate variant in variants_1.png (tiny, logged as polish).

OURS.seen: Bespoke copper atlas and variants; not the vanilla pipe or the industrial sibling.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Sharp at 150 px/cell (assembled_3), with no blur. Variants break the per-cell repeat at irregular spacing (assembled_1). Alignment is clean at every joint. Whether it is 'not bad art' is his taste call, but the specific v2 complaints (blur, repeat) are addressed.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 48 px/cell (assembled_2) it reads clearly as a copper pipe with junction bosses and caps. At 32 px/cell the tube is about 4–5 px, comparable to the industrial sibling, and still reads as a line of copper.

findings.where: variants_1.png, patch-plate variant (horizontal strip near x≈1254 y≈145; vertical cell near x≈1262 y≈550)
findings.seen: A few isolated dark pixel specks float just off the patch plate, outside the tube silhouette. The vertical patch plate also juts slightly past the left tube edge.
findings.quote: Real alpha: no backdrop, halo, water, rock, ground patch or painted shadow under the subject.
findings.fix: The patch-plate variant has fully transparent alpha outside the tube and plate silhouette, and the plate sits symmetrically on the tube.

findings.seen: At normal zoom the wire wraps and patch plates shrink to tiny grey ticks. They break the repeat, but they no longer read as salvage hardware.
findings.quote: Textures are authored at about 128 px per cell; the player sees 32 px per cell in normal play and up to 128–256 px per cell zoomed in. Both must work.
findings.fix: The wire-wrap and patch-plate hardware has slightly higher contrast and length along the tube, so it reads as a distinct band at 32–48 px per cell.

reply.needs_call_why: The owner has rejected this subject twice on taste ('bad art … just bad'). The v2 complaints (blur, per-cell repeat) are measurably fixed, but a clean copper tube may read as tidy plumbing rather than 'salvage/junk-built', and only he can judge that.
proposals: Consider more junk-built character in the base tube (an occasional mismatched section colour, such as a steel or brass sleeve, built into the variant pool) so the Scrapper look reads as salvage rather than new copper plumbing, while keeping the uniform width and seamless joints.
Get an in-game capture from the keeper save when the owner is free, to confirm the offline render matches Graphic_Linked's actual sampling.
